history.sg_progress: In its role as secretariat to the Business Innovations Group, the Development Coordination Office has consistently raised concerns regarding implementation deviations in the efficiency road map with the United Nations Sustainable Development Group and will continue to do so. To support timely follow-up and promote transparency, the Office has developed dashboards for business operations strategy and common premises implementation and is in the process of extending this approach to global shared services and the common back office. These tools enable real-time monitoring and support targeted interventions. Furthermore, the Business Innovations Group, with the support of the Development Coordination Office, is actively refining methodologies and governance mechanisms to address deviations and strengthen the overall implementation of the efficiency road map.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration engage with the United Nations Sustainable Development Group governance to draw attention to and address the gaps in the implementation of the efficiency gains road map in a timely manner.
history.administration_response: The recommendation was implemented. In its capacity as the secretariat of the Business Innovations Group of the United Nations Sustainable Development Group, the Development Coordination Office has supported the Business Innovations Group in its efforts to implement the efficiency gains road map for the period from 2025 to 2028, which was adopted in April 2025. Some of the new tools to draw attention to and address gaps in the implementation of the efficiency gains road map include the global shared services dashboard and the common back office reporting methodology, which are being integrated into UN-Info to provide a unified platform for tracking global shared services and common back office progress alongside the business operations strategy and common premises efficiency workstreams. The Development Coordination Office has also supported the Business Innovations Group in its new “self-starter” common back office approach, empowering resident coordinators to lead local implementation while aligning these efforts with the UN80 Initiative and the milestones of the related work package 14 (unified services road map). Through the formulation of the inter-agency mutual recognition task force and joint collaboration between the common premises and common back office streams, the Development Coordination Office has continued to engage with the United Nations Sustainable Development Group governance to address gaps in implementation and ensure system-wide collaboration and scaling of shared services.
history.board_assessment: Given that the efficiency road map for the period from 2025 to 2028 was adopted in April 2025, new tools such as the global shared services dashboard and the common back office reporting methodology have been introduced to identify and address implementation gaps in the efficiency gains road map, and these tools are also aimed at ensuring system-wide collaboration and scaling of shared services, the Board considers the recommendation to be implemented.
